statement: How many three-digit multiples of $7$ have units digit $3$?

choices.misconception: I thought these numbers come once every $70$ and divided the $900$ three-digit numbers by $70$, getting $12.9$, which I rounded down.
I listed $63, 133, 203, \ldots, 973$ and counted them all, but $63$ is not a three-digit number.
I counted all the three-digit numbers ending in $3$, from $103$ to $993$, without checking which are multiples of $7$.
I counted all the three-digit multiples of $7$, from $105$ to $994$, without checking the units digit.

hints: The units digit of $7k$ depends only on the units digit of $k$.
$7 \cdot 9 = 63$ is the only product $7k$ with $k$ from $0$ to $9$ that ends in $3$. So $k$ must end in $9$.
Three-digit multiples of $7$ are $7k$ with $15 \le k \le 142$. Count the $k$ in that range ending in $9$: $19, 29, \ldots, 139$.

solutions.reliable: A three-digit multiple of $7$ is $7k$ with $15 \le k \le 142$ (since $7 \cdot 15 = 105$ and $7 \cdot 142 = 994$). Its units digit is the units digit of $7$ times the units digit of $k$, and among $7 \cdot 0, 7 \cdot 1, \ldots, 7 \cdot 9$ only $7 \cdot 9 = 63$ ends in $3$. So $k$ ends in $9$: $k = 19, 29, \ldots, 139$, which is $13$ values. The numbers are $133, 203, 273, \ldots, 973$.
solutions.elegant: The numbers ending in $3$ that are multiples of $7$ repeat every $70$: $63, 133, 203, \ldots$. The three-digit ones run from $133$ to $973$, and $(973 - 133) \div 70 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
